title: Check Ignition Gateway System Performance
summary: Use the live Ignition gateway System Performance page in a web browser to inspect CPU and memory trends, database and OPC connectivity, Perspective sessions, system response, current response time, garbage collectors, queued scripts, and recent slow response events during troubleshooting.
when_to_use: Use the live Ignition gateway System Performance page when troubleshooting suspected gateway performance, connectivity, runtime, or response problems and a current view of gateway resource and subsystem indicators is needed.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to infer a numeric healthy threshold; the source provides no numeric thresholds.
Do not use this procedure as a replacement for site or floor confirmation when the symptom requires physical verification.
Do not restart an Ignition or OptiSweep service as part of this procedure; service restart evidence is outside the supplied System Performance procedure.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Open and inspect the Ignition gateway System Performance page and report observable resource, connectivity, session, runtime, and response indicators.
Review escalated gateway performance findings and provide deeper Ignition or platform support when the page is unavailable or indicates an abnormal condition.

safety_notes: This is a read-only diagnostic inspection of the displayed Ignition gateway monitoring information.
Do not infer numeric healthy limits from the displayed trends or values.

access_required: L2 or L3 support access to the Ignition gateway
A web browser capable of opening the Ignition gateway URL
system_preconditions: The Ignition gateway is expected to be reachable for live monitoring information to load.

visual_references.description: Ignition Gateway System Performance page showing CPU Trend, Memory Trend, Database, OPC Connection, Perspective Sessions, System Response, Garbage Collectors, Queuing Scripts, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events.

steps.title: Open the Ignition gateway System Performance page
steps.purpose: Establish a live Ignition gateway view from which the resource, connectivity, runtime, and response indicators can be inspected.
steps.instruction: In a web browser, open the Ignition gateway System Performance page at http://localhost:8088/web/status/sys.performance?2.
steps.expected_result: The Ignition gateway System Performance page opens and displays the named monitoring sections.
steps.healthy_condition: The page is reachable and returns live monitoring information.
steps.failure_condition: The page cannot be opened or does not return live monitoring information.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to deeper Ignition or platform support if the Ignition gateway System Performance page cannot be opened.
Escalate if the page opens but does not return live monitoring information.

source_evidence.evidence: Ignition Gateway UI is accessed through a web browser and displays the System Performance URL.

steps.title: Review CPU Trend and Memory Trend in the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Assess the visible current resource behavior and identify spikes or sustained increases on the live Ignition gateway performance page.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition gateway System Performance page, inspect the CPU Trend and Memory Trend panels. Note the displayed trend shape, visible spikes, and any sustained increase. A memory spike followed by a drop to zero is an observable pattern to report.
steps.expected_result: The current CPU and memory trend behavior is visible and can be reported, including any spike, sustained increase, or drop to zero.
steps.healthy_condition: The CPU Trend and Memory Trend displays are present and do not show an unexplained sustained increase or other abnormal trend during the inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The page shows a visible CPU or memory spike, sustained increase, or a memory pattern such as a spike followed by a drop to zero that correlates with the reported issue.

actions.label: Inspect CPU Trend
actions.exact_action: Review the CPU Trend display on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

actions.label: Inspect Memory Trend
actions.exact_action: Review the Memory Trend display on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if CPU or memory behavior is sustained or abnormal.
Escalate if the displayed memory behavior is consistent with a reported gateway crash or performance symptom.

source_evidence.evidence: The Ignition performance page is used for support; the memory display can show a memory spike followed by a drop to zero.

steps.title: Inspect connectivity and sessions in the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Check the live gateway's displayed database, OPC connection, and Perspective session information for connectivity or session anomalies.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition gateway System Performance page, review the Database, OPC Connection, and Perspective Sessions sections. Record the displayed live state or connection and session information for each section.
steps.expected_result: The Database, OPC Connection, and Perspective Sessions sections display current information that can be reported.
steps.healthy_condition: The three sections are present and show their current live connection or session information without an unexplained unavailable or faulted state.
steps.failure_condition: A Database, OPC Connection, or Perspective Sessions section is unavailable, faulted, or shows an unexpected connection or session state.

actions.label: Inspect Database
actions.exact_action: Review the Database section on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

actions.label: Inspect OPC Connection
actions.exact_action: Review the OPC Connection section on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

actions.label: Inspect Perspective Sessions
actions.exact_action: Review the Perspective Sessions section on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the displayed database, OPC connection, or Perspective session state is unexpected, unavailable, or faulted.

source_evidence.evidence: The Ignition Gateway UI displays Database, OPC Connection, and Perspective Sessions monitoring sections.

steps.title: Review response and runtime activity in the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Identify displayed response-time problems, slow response events, garbage-collector activity, and queued-script activity on the live gateway.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition gateway System Performance page, review System Response, Current Response Time, Recent Slow Response Events, Garbage Collectors, and Queuing Scripts. Record the displayed values or activity, including whether Recent Slow Response Events shows no entries or displays events.
steps.expected_result: The live gateway response and runtime sections can be reported, including current response time, garbage-collector and queued-script information, and the presence or absence of recent slow response events.
steps.healthy_condition: The response and runtime sections return displayed information, and Recent Slow Response Events shows no entries or no unexplained response problem is visible.
steps.failure_condition: The page shows displayed response-time problems, recent slow response events, or an abnormal or unexpected runtime indicator in Garbage Collectors or Queuing Scripts.

actions.label: Inspect system response
actions.exact_action: Review System Response and Current Response Time on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

actions.label: Inspect slow response events
actions.exact_action: Review Recent Slow Response Events and note whether it shows no entries or displays events.

actions.label: Inspect runtime activity
actions.exact_action: Review Garbage Collectors and Queuing Scripts on the Ignition Gateway System Performance page.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the page shows displayed response-time problems.
Escalate if Recent Slow Response Events displays events.
Escalate if Garbage Collectors or Queuing Scripts show unexpected runtime activity.

source_evidence.evidence: The Ignition Gateway UI displays System Response, Garbage Collectors, Queuing Scripts, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events.

steps.title: Report the live Ignition gateway findings
steps.purpose: Create an actionable diagnostic summary from the observable Ignition gateway performance indicators.
steps.instruction: Report the displayed CPU and memory trends; Database, OPC Connection, and Perspective Sessions states; System Response and Current Response Time; Garbage Collectors and Queuing Scripts information; and whether Recent Slow Response Events is empty or contains events. Identify any visible abnormal condition without assigning an unsupported numeric threshold.
steps.expected_result: Support produces a live Ignition gateway finding that distinguishes normal displayed information from visible resource, connectivity, session, response, or runtime abnormalities.
steps.healthy_condition: The report identifies the current displayed values or states and records no unexplained abnormal trend, connection/session state, response indicator, or recent slow response event.
steps.failure_condition: The report identifies one or more visible abnormal CPU, memory, connection, session, response, garbage-collector, queued-script, or slow-response-event findings requiring deeper support.

actions.label: Summarize gateway findings
actions.exact_action: Record the observable results from the Ignition Gateway System Performance page without inferring a numeric healthy threshold.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to deeper Ignition or platform support when the System Performance page is unavailable or does not provide live information.
Escalate when resource, connectivity, session, response, or runtime indicators show an abnormal condition.

source_evidence.evidence: The captured Ignition gateway page provides the named monitoring categories used for the live diagnostic report.

success_criteria: The Ignition gateway System Performance page opens and returns live monitoring information.
CPU Trend and Memory Trend behavior is reported using the displayed trend shape and values.
Database, OPC Connection, and Perspective Sessions states are reported.
System Response, Current Response Time, Garbage Collectors, and Queuing Scripts information is reported.
Recent Slow Response Events is reported as empty or containing events.
Any visible abnormal condition is escalated without inventing a numeric threshold.
healthy_conditions: The Ignition gateway System Performance page is reachable and displays live information.
CPU and memory trends are visible without an unexplained sustained increase or other abnormal pattern.
Database, OPC Connection, and Perspective Sessions sections show current information without an unexpected unavailable or faulted state.
System Response and Current Response Time are displayed without an observed response problem.
Recent Slow Response Events shows no entries.
Garbage Collectors and Queuing Scripts display runtime information without an unexpected condition.
failure_conditions: The Ignition gateway System Performance page cannot be opened or does not return live monitoring information.
CPU or memory shows a visible spike, sustained increase, or other abnormal trend.
Database, OPC Connection, or Perspective Sessions shows an unexpected, unavailable, or faulted state.
System Response or Current Response Time shows a displayed response problem.
Recent Slow Response Events displays events.
Garbage Collectors or Queuing Scripts show unexpected runtime activity.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to deeper Ignition or platform support if the System Performance page cannot be opened or does not return live monitoring information.
Escalate if sustained or abnormal CPU or memory behavior is displayed.
Escalate if database, OPC connection, Perspective session, response-time, garbage-collector, or queued-script information is unexpected.
Escalate if Recent Slow Response Events displays events.
Do not infer numeric healthy thresholds from this procedure.
